title: Time and hardening
short: A correction can remain possible while becoming harder to make useful.
detail: Hardening means increasing difficulty, cost or inequality of correction. It is not automatically irreversibility. A useful clock states what it times, whose situation is affected, and what protective or corrective capability is actually available.
perspective: The same waiting period may be preparation time for one actor and accumulating loss for another.
challenge: Urgency is not proof of irreversibility. Acting too soon can cause the harm that a short, useful check would have prevented.
question: What must happen before which boundary, and what makes that timing credible?
